$comment: R1948 — the analysis tool's SESSIONS section, written down once, in neutral
vocabulary, as the behaviour reference draws it.
THE LAST SEAT. This is the eighth and final destination of the reference's
rail, and the second one this build opens that the SCOPE mockup draws
locked — R1947 opened `topology` the same way and wrote the pattern down.
The mockup books this seat under requirement 18; the BEHAVIOUR reference
builds it, and `docs/analyzer-rail-spec.json`'s `second_phase_owed` has
carried it as the one remaining entry since R1946 measured the gap.
EXTRACTION, measured at the command on 2026-09-01. Two panes: a session
list under a 46-high header carrying the section name, a derived count, a
filter field and three status chips; and a 320-wide detail beside it. The
list is an eight-column grid — session, peer and identifier, link, role,
encryption, uptime, rate, status — over six sessions. The detail carries a
headline, a status pill, the peer it reaches, a four-tile negotiated block,
a handshake timeline and a per-channel sequence list, then two actions.
★★★★★ ONE CAPTURE, TWO SECTIONS. Every session names a PEER, and those are
the same six the topology section plots: the reference's detail pane has a
control that jumps to the graph with that peer selected. That is not a
coincidence to reproduce loosely — it is the reason both sections are views
of one capture rather than two screens that happen to sit on one rail, and
this build asserts it (`tests::r1948_every_session_names_a_peer_the_
topology_plots`). Requiring it is what stops the two populations drifting.
VOCABULARY. Neutral throughout and consistent with the sibling sections:
the peers are `P-01`..`P-06` as `hello-topology-view` declares them, and
the handshake steps are named for what they do rather than for the
reference's own wire words.
THE TWO HALVES, as in every sibling pin: `canon` is what the reference
draws, `owed` is where this build does not draw it yet. The gate asserts
the difference between the painted surface and `canon` is EXACTLY `owed`.
The left pane. The header's second run is a COUNT the reference states
as `5 active / 1 closed`, and this build derives both halves from the
population rather than writing them — a count beside a list it does not
come from is the defect this tree has found repeatedly.
`rows` is the grid as one surface. Its interior — a session's eight
cells — is not enumerated here on purpose: those are a population that
changes with the capture, and a specification that listed them would be
a copy of the data rather than of the screen. `painted.rs` asserts every
declared session is drawn and reaches its own detail.
The right pane, 320 wide. What the reference shows about the session a
reader picked.
★ `topology` is the reference's own control OUT of this section, and it
WORKS here rather than refusing: R1947 built the section it leads to, so
this is the first cross-section action in this application. `close` is
the reference's destructive control and is drawn and refused, which is
this tree's treatment of an affordance nothing has built.
